title: Derived direct image between Noetherian schemes has a right adjoint on quasi-coherent complexes
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of Noetherian schemes (schemes [def-pc-scheme] that are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), and let $Rf_*:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_Y)$ be the derived direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Then $Rf_*$ maps the full subcategory $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves [def-pc-derived-category] into $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, and the restricted functor $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ has a right adjoint.

source.place: Tag 0A9E (duality-lemma-twisted-inverse-image), stated there for a morphism of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes; the first clause is Tag 08DW part (1) (perfect-lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-image, perfect.tex), for quasi-compact quasi-separated f. Noetherian schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated

proof.text: A Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact by definition and quasi-separated because it is locally Noetherian; apply the existing quasi-separatedness statement to both X and Y.

By step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1) (X quasi-compact and Y quasi-separated give f quasi-compact; X quasi-separated gives f quasi-separated), f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Hence [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh] shows that Rf_* sends D_QCoh(O_X) into D_QCoh(O_Y); this is the first clause of the statement, and it makes the restricted functor Rf_*:D_QCoh(O_X)\to D_QCoh(O_Y) used in steps 5 and 6 well defined.
For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme X, the category D_QCoh(O_X) has set-indexed direct sums.
For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme X, D_QCoh(O_X) is compactly generated.
Since f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (step 2), Rf_* on quasi-coherent derived categories preserves set-indexed direct sums.

Brown representability applied to the exact functor Rf_*:D_QCoh(O_X)\to D_QCoh(O_Y) now supplies a right adjoint: both categories have set-indexed direct sums by step 3 (applied to X and to Y), the source is compactly generated by step 4, and Rf_* preserves direct sums by step 5.
